name: Dropbear SSH Repo
description: Standalone KPM repository for the dropbear-ssh package (on-demand SSH/SFTP over WiFi for jailbroken Kindles)

dropbear-ssh.name: Dropbear SSH
dropbear-ssh.author: Akshay
dropbear-ssh.description: On-demand SSH/SFTP server (dropbear, repackaged from notmarek/kindle-usbnetlite) over your existing WiFi — no USB networking needed. Launching opens a status app with a Start/Stop button (talks to a small loopback-only HTTP bridge on-device, no external server) showing the connect command and password while running, plus a "Keep reachable while Kindle sleeps" checkbox — defers the device's own suspend cycle (confirmed via powerd's readyToSuspend event + powerd_test -d) so the server stays reachable through sleep instead of WiFi getting suspended with it; costs more battery (WiFi/CPU stay active), the screen itself costs nothing either way. The server also correctly keeps running after closing the app (previously it didn't — confirmed and fixed via setsid), and reopening the app no longer kills it either — confirmed the hard way that kpm install always restarts the server on every call even when nothing changed, so the launcher scriptlet now only installs on a genuinely fresh install, not on every tap. The app now also has a "Check for Update" button — installs whatever's currently latest, honestly reports whether anything actually changed (comparing installed version before/after, since kpm itself always claims "upgrading" even for an identical reinstall), and restarts the server afterward if it was running, via a separate detached script rather than inline since kpm install replaces the app's own files including whichever script triggered it; the app polls for the real result instead of asking you to reopen it. Update also now restarts the loopback bridge and the keep-awake loop if either was running — uninstall.sh (which every kpm install runs first) unconditionally kills both, unrelated to whether the SSH server itself was running, so without this every tap of Check for Update silently broke every other button until the Home-screen icon was retapped. A random password is generated on install and printed in the KPM log; set your own any time by editing /mnt/us/usbnetlite/etc/ssh_password and restarting the server, or now directly in the app — a password field and Set Password button write it and restart the server for you if it's running. The keep-awake checkbox is also now a much larger tap target (was 24px, genuinely too small to hit reliably), and the whole row responds to a tap, not just the checkbox itself. A real update now reloads the page automatically afterward — confirmed the hard way that a genuine version change can add new UI elements that just don't appear until the page is actually reloaded. Stopping the server now also turns off keep-awake if it was on — it exists purely to keep the server reachable through sleep, so leaving it on with no server to keep reachable was pure battery cost for no benefit. Verified working on Kindle PaperWhite 4 (kernel 4.1.x), Kindle Paperwhite 5 (kernel 4.9.77), and a Kindle Paperwhite 6 (Véra jailbreak, kernel 5.15.x). Ships a second binary build for newer/older devices per upstream's own release split, selected automatically by kernel version at install time — that second build now also bundles libcrypt.so.1 for newer Kindle firmware that doesn't ship it system-wide, a known issue shared with KOReader's own SSH plugin.
